newsitem.title: USA: Apple CEO says turnaround plan on track.
newsitem.headline: Apple CEO says turnaround plan on track.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. said Tuesday the computer maker's three-year turnaround plan was still on track despite its statement last week that it will report a first-quarter operating loss of as much as $150 million.

Apple Chairman Gilbert Amelio, giving the keynote address for the 13th annual MacWorld Conference here, said the first-quarter shortfall was due largely to market conditions rather than a problem with the company.
He said Apple's cash position remains at around $1.7 billion.
"We're in a good position," Amelio said, referring to the Cupertino, Calif.-based company's financial resources.
The first quarter "was about retail sales, not about the fundamentals in the recovery of Apple," Amelio told a packed ballroom here.

"We had one thing that really fell out of bed in a big way and that is, Santa Claus forgot to come," he said, referring to the surprisingly low sales of its Performa desktop PC line aimed at consumers.

Although the financial shortfall was a disappointment, Amelio said it would not require any change in the company's turnaround plan and that all of the strategic decisions made under his leadership were still applicable.

Amelio moved from National Semiconductor Corp. to become became chairman of Apple last February, taking control of a company swamped by heavy losses, layoffs and numerous high-level management departures.
"The three-year plan that I've been talking about since May is still solid," Amelio said. Under the plan, Apple seeks to return to sustainable profits in 1998.
Amelio encouraged software developers and customers not to give up hope despite the first-quarter setback.
Amelio likened the company's problems to an aircraft encountering rough weather.
"It's sort of like hitting one of those air pockets in turbulence," he said. "It's not going to change our course."
Apple's stock edged down 12.5 cents to $17.75 on Nasdaq in late trading.
